result.title: Forget the Data, Keep the Capability: Switchable Unlearning for Retrieval
result.summary: Privacy compliance requires re-identification models to selectively forget individuals while preserving their ability to recognize others. For this, we present MoME, a switchable framework that can adapt pre-trained backbones for privacy compliance, allowing the same model to switch between Full mode for standard inference and Core mode for unlearned inference. MoME splits one backbone into core parameters that preserve retrieval and zero-initialized parasitic parameters that carry the full-data knowledge, and training them under gradient isolation so the core never receives a forget-set gradient. Disabling the branch yields Core, which satisfies a request to delete a person's training data, and enabling it yields Full, which retains what the deleted data taught, so honoring the request is a flag flip rather than a retraining run. We prove Core independent of the forget set up to an audited set of coupling channels and introduce the rank-based Forgetting-Rank statistic to audit that independence in a trained model. On Market-1501, VeRi-776 and RegDB, Core reads at a retrained reference under three membership attacks while retrieving above it, and the retrieval advantage carries to ResNet and CLIP backbones. Code and weights are available at https://github.com/Jingong-Chen/MoME.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 MoME 可切换框架：将预训练检索骨干拆成保留检索能力的 core 参数与零初始化的 parasitic 分支承载全量知识，用梯度隔离训练，从而以开关而非重训来满足删除请求，并提出 rank-based Forgetting-Rank 统计量审计两分支的独立性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「零初始化旁支 + 梯度隔离 + 审计耦合通道」的做法可供核查是否可用于分离与审计 VLM 中真正供给答案的视觉通路，即判断 latent 内容是否被实际使用，但该工作本身不涉及多模态推理或 latent 状态生成。
